author: Zimm, Alan D.
title: Attack on Pearl Harbor: Strategy, Combat, Myths, Deceptions
notes: An operations analyst's reconstruction of the attack — weapons effects, target selection, the arithmetic of what the aircraft carried against what they hit — and the standard modern statement of the case that the third wave is a myth: that no third strike was in the plan, that the fuel tanks were not the soft target they are described as, and that the conference on Akagi's bridge at which Fuchida is said to have urged one did not happen as he told it. **Not read.** No copy could be opened from this environment. What this registry knows of the argument comes from a signed review by Charles C. Kolb for the Naval Historical Foundation, and the bibliographic detail — publisher, city, year, 464 pages — comes from that review rather than from the item. No ISBN is recorded, for the reason given in docs/sources.md. Where the pack states Zimm's position it says on the card that it is stated at second hand.
